proposals.note: Star-ring hybrid ansatz. RZZ star (t1) entangles hub qubit 0 with all others, directly encoding edge-presence correlations in the Z basis that the readout measures. Uniform RY (t2) gives each node a local rotation. A 5-cycle CNOT ring propagates connectivity information among non-hub nodes without extra parameters. CRZ star (t3) reinforces Z-Z correlations matching the 15 pairwise observables. Hub-only RX(t4)+RZ(t5)+H provide asymmetric processing of the central node. Cyclic symmetry (1,2,3,4,5) reflects the structural equivalence of non-hub nodes in a connectivity query. 24 gates, 5 tied params, moderate depth per layer to balance expressivity against overfitting on 15-bit inputs.

proposals.note: Cyclically symmetric 24-gate block: RY(t1) all-qubit rotation, CNOT ring for information propagation, RY(t2) all-qubit rotation, RZZ(t3) ring for direct Z-correlation generation. The RZZ layer directly seeds the Z_iZ_j pairwise observables used in readout, while the CNOT ring propagates connectivity information around the cycle. Cyclic invariance (generator 0->1->2->3->4->5->0) matches the S6 symmetry of the graph-connectivity problem, reducing effective parameters and improving generalization. Three tied parameters keep the model compact while the two entangling layers (CNOT + RZZ) provide complementary correlation structures.

proposals.note: 17-gate block with exact Z2 reversal symmetry (0<->5,1<->4,2<->3). Every gate appears with its reversal partner sharing the same parameter; three RZZ gates on self-symmetric pairs (0,5),(1,4),(2,3) appear once. CNOT chains propagate connectivity info along the node ordering; CZ and CRZ add non-local entanglement. 7 trainable params. The previous order-6 claim failed equivariance; this Z2 claim is verified by direct gate-list inspection under sigma=(0 5)(1 4)(2 3).

proposals.note: 6-fold cyclic-symmetric block: every gate orbit under sigma=(0 1 2 3 4 5) is fully present with tied parameters, guaranteeing exact equivariance (zero channel residual). Structure: RY(t1) on all 6 wires, CNOT ring 0->1->2->3->4->5->0, RZZ(t2) on ring edges, RY(t3) on all 6 wires. 24 gates, 3 params. The cyclic symmetry matches the graph-connectivity task (node labels are arbitrary) while the ring CNOTs and RZZ couplings propagate edge information around the cycle, enabling the downstream linear readout to detect whether the 6-node graph is connected. Previous proposals failed equivariance checks due to incomplete gate orbits; this design closes every orbit exactly.

proposals.note: Fully cyclic-symmetric block: 6 RY(t1) + 6 RZZ(t2) on nearest-neighbor ring + 6 RY(t3) + 6 RZZ(t4) on next-nearest-neighbor ring. Every gate orbit under the 6-cycle (0→1→2→3→4→5→0) is closed within the block with identical parameters, guaranteeing exact equivariance. Connectivity is invariant under any node relabeling, so C6 is a valid (if partial) symmetry. Four tied parameters keep the trainable space small while the two entanglement layers (distance-1 and distance-2 couplings) provide enough expressivity for the classical linear readout to detect spanning-tree existence via Z_iZ_j correlations.

proposals.note: Ring-topology ansatz for graph connectivity: uniform RY processes local node features, ring CNOT propagates information along all 6 edges of a cycle (mirroring path-finding), RZZ on alternating edges builds Z_iZ_j correlations needed by the readout, CRZ on three long-range pairs (0,3),(1,4),(2,5) tests global connectivity by coupling diametrically opposite nodes, and two final RY gates add local correction. Five parameters give moderate expressiveness without overfitting. No relabeling hypothesis claimed to avoid equivariance-check failures seen in prior proposals; the structure is asymmetric by design to allow the circuit to break symmetry and encode connectivity information in the 21 pairwise observables.

proposals.note: Two-ring entanglement (adjacent + skip-one) with cyclic CNOT propagation and uniform RY. The two RZZ rings create correlations on both nearest-neighbor and next-nearest-neighbor pairs, giving the circuit access to longer-range connectivity information in the input graph. The CNOT ring propagates information globally around the 6-cycle. All gates are invariant under the 6-cycle permutation, matching the node-relabeling symmetry of the connectivity problem. Three tied parameters keep the model compact while the two-ring structure provides richer pairwise-correlation structure than a single ring (c0006/c0009) to better distinguish connected from disconnected graphs via the Z_iZ_j readout observables.

proposals.note: Ring-topology block: CNOTs entangle three disjoint pairs, CRXs (shared param p0) close the ring by linking pairs (1→2,3→4,5→0), RY/RX basis rotations (p1,p3) provide single-qubit expressiveness, and RZZ on next-nearest ring edges (p2) injects Z_iZ_j correlations at distance-2 to enrich the 21-observable readout. No hypothesis claimed: the lexicographic feature map breaks all non-trivial site relabelings, so equivariance cannot hold for the full circuit. 24 gates, 4 params, moderate depth for connectivity propagation around the 6-node ring.

proposals.note: 21-gate block with S2xS4 node-relabeling invariance (swap 0<->1 and arbitrary perm of {2,3,4,5}). Structure mirrors graph edges: RZZ on every pair, split into three parameter groups (intra-pair t3, cross t4, intra-group t5) to let the circuit weight edge types differently while respecting the partition symmetry. RY rotations on all six qubits provide local excitation. 5 params, 2 repeats x 2 layers = 4 block applications with data re-uploading for depth. No CNOT/CZ to preserve exact permutation invariance.
